title: CI blocked at scheduling by GitHub billing: fix in account Settings → Billing & plans
description: All 5 CI runs (including run 1 on the bootstrap commit) fail in ~3s with no runner and no steps. Signature of the repository Actions policy rejecting third-party actions (dtolnay/rust-toolchain, Swatinem/rust-cache, j178/prek-action). Fix: actions/checkout + actions/cache only; install toolchain via rustup from rust-toolchain.toml; install prek with pipx. If runs still fail identically after this, the cause is account-level (Actions disabled or billing) and must be fixed in repository settings.

Left open for the account owner: fix Billing & plans, then Actions → CI → Re-run jobs on main. First real CI run may surface runner issues (pipx install prek, cache paths); handle then.

title: Layered configuration: file, environment, command line
description:
The binary is configured by environment variables and a few flags, read in six different places. That works for one laptop and breaks in Kubernetes, where shape (URLs, thresholds, rubric text, team list) belongs in a ConfigMap under review, secrets belong in a Secret, and an operator needs to know which value won.

Deliver one configuration model with an explicit precedence, lowest to highest: built-in default, configuration file (TOML), environment variable, command-line flag. Every environment read moves into one module so the precedence table in the docs is the code. Secrets (API keys, tokens, webhook secret) are never accepted from the file.

Also move what was compiled but is really configuration into the file: policy thresholds, the fallback team list, the impact rubric, and the text of every question. The set of questions and their types stay in code: the policy consumes them and the typed handles exist to keep that contract honest.
close_reason: All children delivered; follow-ups are ordinary settings additions through the documented three-place rule.

title: Decision 0005: observability signals enter through incident.io, no direct Tsuga client
description: Record the Tsuga assessment as a MADR decision. Evidence: Tsuga's OpenAPI spec exists at GET https://api.tsuga.com/v0/open-api (and /v0/internal-open-api) but answers 401 without an operation API key; nothing public documents it. The web app's bundles show POST /v0/alerts/ongoing/query with filters (owners, searchQuery, priorities, clusterIds, triggeredBy key:value dimensions, types monitor|slo) sorted by priority; a service catalog under /v0/service-catalog; and a native incident.io notification integration. Options weighed: direct Tsuga client from the reverse-engineered contract; Tsuga alerts forwarded into incident.io by Tsuga's own integration and read back through GET /v2/alerts; both. Chosen: through incident.io, consistent with decision 0001. Revisit when an operation API key allows reading the spec (deferred child).

title: Related firing alerts as blast-radius context
description:
An alert is qualified faster when the responder and the model see what else is firing. Fetch firing alerts created within a window (GET /v2/alerts?status[one_of]=firing&created_at[gte]=<now-window>, page_size 50), exclude the alert itself, cap the list (20), and add them to the state as alert.related_alerts with title, age in minutes and the component label when present. Reference the path in the impact question guidance (several alerts on the same component or its dependents indicate broader impact) and in the dedup question. List them in the qualification note.

Observability alerts from Tsuga reach this list through Tsuga's native incident.io notification integration; no Tsuga client is added (decision 0005).

Acceptance: state contains related_alerts in the wiremock e2e test; window configurable with SIGNALMAN_RELATED_WINDOW_MINUTES (default 30); a failure to list related alerts degrades to an empty list with a warning.

title: Qualification note on the incident.io alert
description:
Tags encode the verdict but not the reasoning, the confidence, or where to look next. A responder still opens Backstage, the runbook and the incident list by hand. Post one markdown note on the alert (POST /v1/alert_notes, alert_id) that carries everything the tags imply plus what they cannot: owner with confidence and the confirm-owner flag, impact level with its distribution, actionable probability, the matched incident with permalink, suspected change, the resolved catalog component and owner group as Backstage links, the TechDocs runbook page link, the upstream alert link, related firing alerts, and the time to qualify.

Rules: deterministic template in code (decision 0002: no generated text). Exactly one signalman note per alert: list existing notes (GET /v1/alert_notes?alert_id=) and PUT the existing one when its first line carries the signalman marker, so retriage rewrites in place instead of stacking. Respect WriteBack::DryRun. A note failure is logged and must not undo tags or attachments. Backstage links need BACKSTAGE_APP_URL (frontend), defaulting to BACKSTAGE_BASE_URL.

Acceptance: wiremock test asserts the note body and the create-or-replace behaviour; Outcome gains note_id; docs updated (incident.io page, configuration).
close_reason: Implemented on claude/rust-typesafe-api-zf13d9: note.rs, related alerts in sync.rs, time_to_qualify, decision 0005, docs

title: Reduce mean time to qualify (MTTQ)
description:
Mean time to qualify: the time from an alert being created in incident.io to the moment a responder has, in one place, the answers to five questions: is it actionable, who owns it, how bad is it, is it already a known incident, and did something change. signalman already computes those judgments; the gap is that they surface only as tags, without the reasoning, the links or the surrounding context, and that nobody measures the interval.

Scope, deliberately small (Unix rule: few things, done well):
1. One qualification note on the alert in incident.io, rewritten in place, with judgments, links (incident, Backstage component and owner group, TechDocs runbook, upstream alert) and the time to qualify.
2. Other firing alerts in the window as blast-radius context, in the model state and in the note.
3. Time to qualify measured per alert (alert created_at to decision) in the outcome, logs and note.
4. Decision record: observability signals (Tsuga) enter through incident.io; no direct Tsuga client until the spec is verified with an operation API key.

Out of scope, recorded as deferred children: on-call lookup through incident.io schedules; a direct Tsuga client.

Knowing who is on call for the owning group removes the 'who do I ping' step. incident.io exposes GET /v2/schedules/{id} with current shifts; Backstage groups can carry an annotation (for example incident.io/schedule-id) mapping the group to a schedule, in the spirit of the @incident-io/backstage plugin's catalog mapping. Implement only once the note and related alerts are in use and the mapping convention is agreed with the on-call leads.

title: Handle private alerts in the webhook flow
description: private_alert.alert_created_v1 carries only the id. With an API key that has private access, fetch and triage like public alerts; otherwise log and skip. Currently ignored silently.

title: Forward alert resolved events with --forward-to-incidentio
description: CLI forwarding only sends status=firing. Accept a status field in the alert JSON and send resolved with the same deduplication_key so the incident.io alert auto-resolves.

value: Architecture rule (decision signalman-p2w, docs/decisions/0001): incident.io stays the alert hub. signalman only writes alert tags (ai-team-*, ai-impact-*, ai-action-*, ai-dup-*, ai-suspected-change), POST /v2/incident_alerts attachments, and one qualification note per alert (/v1/alert_notes, marker line '**Signalman qualification**', replaced in place on retriage), or feeds an HTTP alert source with judgments under metadata.ai. Never create incidents directly; alert routes own that.

Recent changes (decision 0007, src/changes.rs): delivery tools POST /changes (bearer SIGNALMAN_CHANGES_TOKEN, secret env only; unset = route absent) with {kind, summary, component?, at?, source?, url?}. ChangeLog is in-memory per replica (1000 newest). Triage offers changes matching component hints or platform-wide within flow.change_window_minutes (default 120, SIGNALMAN_CHANGE_WINDOW_MINUTES), cap flow.change_max (10), only when the alert carried no recent_changes itself. No client for Argo CD/Flux/GitHub; wiring is templates on their side (docs/changes.md).

Configuration precedence (decision 0006, src/config.rs): built-in default < TOML file (--config, SIGNALMAN_CONFIG, ./signalman.toml, /etc/signalman/config.toml) < environment variable < flag. config.rs is the only module reading non-secret env vars; secrets (TYPESAFE_API_KEY, INCIDENTIO_API_KEY, INCIDENTIO_WEBHOOK_SECRET, BACKSTAGE_TOKEN) are env only and refused from the file. [policy], [triage.text], [[triage.teams]] are file-only. Every new setting: schema in Settings, resolve in Config::resolve, row in docs/configuration.md (tests/config_precedence.rs checks ENV_VARS appear in the doc).

GitHub Actions on this repository never ran: every job is refused at scheduling with the billing annotation ('recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased'). Check-run annotations are readable unauthenticated at api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo>/check-runs/<id>/annotations. Nothing in the repo fixes this; the account owner must fix Billing & plans, then re-run. Tracked as signalman-oqj.

incident.io contract: OpenAPI v3 at https://api.incident.io/v1/openapiV3.json (the /v1/openapi.json endpoint is removed, returns 410); guides at https://docs.incident.io/llms.txt; webhooks guide at https://docs.incident.io/api-reference/webhooks.md. Webhooks are Svix-signed (webhook-id/-timestamp/-signature, HMAC-SHA256 over id.ts.body, secret is base64 after whsec_). src/incidentio/webhook.rs is pinned to Svix's published test vector.

Laya (huggingface convaiinnovations/laya, Apache 2.0, pip laya, 421M ModernBERT-large) implements the System One wire shape (state + noul/choice/score questions -> answers with probabilities/confidence, extra 'rl_agent' key ignored by serde). signalman runs unchanged against a shim (examples/laya/serve_laya.py) via typesafe.base_url; TYPESAFE_API_KEY must be set but is ignored by the shim. Zero-shot on our alerts it is weak (every impact Major, owner confidence <0.5, 2-6 s/request on 4 CPUs); the model card says fine-tune first. Evaluation tracked in beads under signalman-ufg.

Nothing has been run against a real TypeSafe or incident.io account yet (no keys in the dev container). Epic signalman-b11 tracks live verification; the multi-value status_category[one_of] repeated-key filter (signalman-b11.3) is the most likely drift point.

Project renamed from rustsafe to signalman on 2026-09-20 (crate, binary, CLI, env var SIGNALMAN_ADDR, docs, beads prefix). The GitHub repository must be renamed by the owner to chussenot/signalman; git redirects keep the old URL working.

Quality gates before any push: cargo fmt --all --check; RUSTFLAGS=-D warnings cargo clippy --all-targets (pedantic, unwrap_used); cargo test (no network: wiremock mocks both APIs); RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc --no-deps. Product names allowed in docs via clippy.toml doc-valid-idents.

Tsuga (observability, tsuga.com): no public API spec. GET https://api.tsuga.com/v0/open-api exists but needs an operation API key (401 otherwise). Web bundles evidence POST /v0/alerts/ongoing/query (filters owners, searchQuery, priorities, clusterIds, triggeredBy key:value, types monitor|slo). Decision 0005 (signalman-3l7.4): Tsuga alerts enter through Tsuga's native incident.io integration and are read back as related firing alerts; no Tsuga client until the spec is read (signalman-3l7.6).

TypeSafe docs are the API contract: start at https://docs.typesafe.ai/llms.txt; API reference at /api.md; append .md to any page path for markdown. No Rust SDK exists; src/client.rs mirrors the Python SDK defaults (jev-latest, 10s timeout, 2 retries 0.5s→5s, retry on 408/429/5xx, honour Retry-After).
